title: Coefficient sheaves on the geometric point
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be separably closed and $X=\Spec\Omega$. For a condensed set or
condensed ring $F$, $(p_X^*F)(\Omega[S])\cong F(S)$ naturally in the profinite set
$S$. In particular:

1. for a topological ring $T$ (for instance profinite or locally profinite),
   $\underline T_X(\Omega[S])=C(S,T)$, the continuous functions;
2. for a discrete ring $A$, $\underline A_X(\Omega[S])=LC(S,A)=\varinjlim_iA^{S_i}$,
   which is $(\nu_X^*A_{X,\Et})(\Omega[S])$; so $\underline A_X$ is the classical
   constant sheaf.

proof.text: Use the existing field-independent testFullyFaithful, testTopologyReflect and testCoverPreserving helpers in GeometricFieldProfiniteDenseSubsite, whose spectrum calculations use [lem-weil-pbc-locally-constant-prime-spectrum]. The affine ind-etale equivalence in [det-pe-condensed-point-basis] identifies every affine basis object with a profinite test object. Cover density follows from [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis]. Apply [lem-pc-fppf-dense-sheaf-equivalence] to obtain equivalence of restriction on sets and abelian groups. The specified set adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback] has invertible unit, giving set evaluation. For rings lift the monoidal adjunction unit of [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point] to monoid objects, using the canonical monoidal pushforward-composition comparison. This identifies the specified [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] with the original ring after restriction.

Specialize ring evaluation to the continuous coefficient sheaf. The sheafification counit transporting its ring structure recovers the original pointwise presheaf ring. For discrete A the identity on functions is a ring equivalence from locally constant to continuous functions. A locally constant function factors through its discrete quotient. Surjectivity of every quotient projection makes each cocone leg injective. The filtered-colimit criterion in types, and reflection by the ring forgetful functor, prove the asserted ring colimit, including the empty space.

Apply the proved discrete constant-ring comparison theorem for the final two clauses and combine the four conjuncts. Its proof uses the canonical monoidal constant-sheaf pullback comparison and locally bijective sheafification, with no residual holes.

proof_origin.place: Both paragraphs formalized: dense restriction, monoidal adjunction unit, filtered colimits, and the fully proved discrete constant-ring comparison.
